abstract: BACKGROUND: To assess the ability of [(18)F]fluorodeoxyglucose (F-18 FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) to predict the viability of residual masses after chemotherapy in patients with metastatic nonseminomatous germ cell tumors (GCT), PET results were compared in a blinded analysis with computed tomography (CT) scans and serum tumor marker changes (TUM) as established methods of assessment. METHODS: Independent reviewers who were blinded to each other's results evaluated the PET results and corresponding CT scan and TUM results in 85 residual lesions from 45 patients. All patients were treated within prospective clinical trials and received primary/salvage, high-dose chemotherapy with autologous blood stem cell support for primary poor prognosis disease or recurrent disease. PET results were assessed both visually and by quantifying glucose uptake (standardized uptake values). Results were validated either by histologic examination of a resected mass and/or biopsy (n = 28 lesions) or by a 6-month clinical follow-up after evaluation (n = 57 lesions). RESULTS: F-18 FDG PET showed increased tracer uptake in 32 of 85 residual lesions, with 29 true positive (TP) lesions and three false positive (FP) lesions. Fifty-three lesions were classified by PET as negative (no viable GCT), 33 lesions were classified by PET as true negative (TN), and 20 lesions were classified by PET as false negative (FN). In the blinded reading of the corresponding CT scan and TUM results, 38 residual lesions were assessed correctly as containing viable carcinoma and/or teratoma. Forty-six lesions were classified as non-suspicious by CT scan/TUM (33 TN lesions and 14 falsely classified lesions). PET correctly predicted the presence of viable carcinoma in 5 of these 14 and the absence of viable carcinoma in 3 of these 14 lesions. Resulting sensitivities and specificities for the prediction of residual mass viability were as follows: PET, 59% sensitivity and 92% specificity; radiologic monitoring, 55% sensitivity and 86% specificity; and TUM, 42% sensitivity and 100% specificity. The positive and negative predictive values for PET were 91% and 62%, respectively. The diagnostic efficacy of PET did not improve when patients with teratomatous elements in the primary tumor were excluded from the analysis. In patients with multiple residual masses, a uniformly increased residual F-18 FDG uptake in all lesions was a strong predictor for the presence of viable carcinoma. CONCLUSIONS: F-18 FDG PET imaging performed in conjunction with conventional staging methods offers additional information for the prediction of residual mass histology in patients with nonseminomatous GCT. A positive PET is highly predictive for the presence of viable carcinoma. Other useful indications for a PET examination include patients with multiple residual masses and patients with marker negative disease.
abstract_ja: 背景：転移性非セミノーマ性胚細胞腫瘍の患者において、化学療法後の残存腫瘤の生存（viable）腫瘍の有無を予測する[18F]FDG陽電子放射断層撮影(PET)の能力を、従来の評価法であるコンピュータ断層撮影(CT)および血清腫瘍マーカーの変化（TUM）と比較した。方法：独立した2名の読影者が、互いの結果を知らされない状態で、45例の患者の85病変について、PET結果と対応するCTおよびTUMの結果を評価した。対象患者は、前向き臨床試験の中で、予後不良な初発疾患または再発疾患に対して、初回または救援の大量化学療法と自家末梢血幹細胞支持療法を受けていた。PET所見は視覚的評価と、グルコース取り込みの定量（標準化取り込み値）の両方で評価した。結果は、切除腫瘤および／または生検の病理学的検査（28病変）、または評価後6か月の臨床的フォローアップ（57病変）によって検証した。結果：F-18 FDG PETでは85病変中32病変に集積の増加を認め、そのうち29病変は真陽性（TP）、3病変は偽陽性（FP）であった。53病変はPETで陰性（生存腫瘍なし）と判定され、そのうち33病変は真陰性（TN）、20病変は偽陰性（FN）であった。盲検で読影したCTおよびTUMの結果では、38病変が生存癌腫および／または奇形腫を含むと正しく評価された。46病変はCT／TUMで疑わしくないと判定され（うち33病変はTN、14病変は誤判定）、PETはこの14病変のうち5病変で生存癌の存在を、3病変で生存癌の不在を正しく予測した。PETの感度と特異度は次のとおりであった：PET 59%の感度と92%の特異度、放射線学的モニタリング 55%の感度と86%の特異度、TUM 42%の感度と100%の特異度。PETの陽性的中率と陰性的中率はそれぞれ91%と62%であった。原発腫瘍に奇形腫成分を有する患者を解析から除外しても、PETの診断能は改善しなかった。複数の残存腫瘤を有する患者では、すべての病変で残存FDG集積が一様に増加していることが、生存癌の存在の強い予測因子であった。結論：従来の病期分類法と併用して行うF-18 FDG PET画像検査は、非セミノーマ性GCT患者の残存腫瘤の組織型予測に追加情報を提供する。PET陽性は生存癌の存在を強く予測する。PET検査の他の有用な適応として、複数の残存腫瘤を有する患者と、腫瘍マーカー陰性疾患の患者が挙げられる。
